audit.summary: The current SCOUT pseudocode inspects a leaf before its empty-window guard, while the finite-cost proof assigns zero cost to that state. An exact legal tree violates the finite prefactor-one inequality; a factor-two comparison preserves the main asymptotic upper bound.

repair.content: Check the empty window before reading a leaf to match the proof. Alternatively, for nonempty full windows \(n\ge1\), every extra read can be charged to a preceding TEST read, giving printed cost at most twice corrected cost. That fixed factor preserves the asymptotic upper growth bound when limits exist; it does not restore the finite prefactor one.
